subject: Evidence archival scope & escrow: clarifying post-incident retention
messages:
From: Acme Health Security Ops <security_ops@acmehealth.com>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwoodinference.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: forensics@secureaudit.io
Date: Tue, 05 Jun 2028 08:14:00 -0700
Subject: Post-incident logs — retention window and escrow option

Hi Priya / Marcus,

Thanks again for the quick help during the incident last week. Acme's legal and security teams need clarification on two items before we close our internal post-incident review:

1) How long will Redwood retain full-fidelity request/response logs and associated KV cache snapshots for our tenant under the standard incident hold?
2) Do you offer an evidence-escrow option (transfer to an agreed third-party cold store) and if so what is the process, timeline, and required paperwork?

We're preparing an audit package and would like a short write-up we can include in the binder. If you can also provide a sample manifest of what a transferred set looks like (schema + hashing approach), that would be very helpful.

Attachments: acme_incident_summary.pdf

Appreciate it —
Security Ops (Acme Health)
security_ops@acmehealth.com
From: Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwoodinference.com>
To: Acme Health Security Ops <security_ops@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>, Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwoodinference.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 05 Jun 2028 10:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Post-incident logs — retention window and escrow option

Thanks — and sorry for the disruption on your side. Short answers up front: we can hold full-fidelity artifacts for a default 90-day forensic retention window after an incident, and we support an evidence-escrow transfer to a named third-party under an executed agreement.

Details / proposed approach:
- Retention: Redwood will place an administrative hold on the complete incident bucket (raw request/response logs, KV cache snapshots, and trace slices) for 90 days by default. That hold prevents automated deletion and is accessible to our SRE/forensics team.
- Escrow transfer: we can stage a hashed, immutable bundle and transfer either to a SecureAudit AWS S3 bucket (cross-account) or export to an encrypted archive for customer-controlled escrow. We need a signed Evidence Transfer Agreement and a POA for transfer if a third-party acts on your behalf.
- Manifest: attaching a sample manifest (log_sample_manifest.csv) that shows file names, timestamps, SHA256 hashes, and sample sizes. We also include a short checklist of what we retain vs what we omit (PII redaction rules for extracts).

Next steps I propose:
1) Acme confirms desired escrow recipient (SecureAudit or Acme-controlled bucket) and acceptance of the 90-day hold.
2) Redwood sends an Evidence Transfer Agreement draft for signature.
3) Marcus will provide the technical manifest and a timeline for a staged transfer (typically 3–5 business days once agreement is signed).

I'll coordinate the draft agreement with Mina (legal) in parallel.

Best,
Priya Natarajan
Head of Security Partnerships | Redwood Inference
+1 (415) 555-0123
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwoodinference.com>, Acme Health Security Ops <security_ops@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 05 Jun 2028 14:28:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Post-incident logs — retention window and escrow option

Folks — adding the technical pieces you asked for. High level:

- What we keep: raw request/response pairs (rotating hourly files), KV cache snapshots (per model session id), scheduler traces, and sampling metadata. For large multimedia payloads we keep metadata and a pointer to the binary store; full binary retention is possible under escrow request.
- Manifest schema: columns are file_path, start_ts, end_ts, sha256, file_size_bytes, record_count, compressed(true/false). See attached log_sample_manifest.csv.
- Hashing & verification: we compute SHA256 at rest. For escrow transfers we publish a signed transfer manifest and provide pre-signed S3 URLs for SecureAudit to ingest; cross-account copy maintains object metadata and includes a transfer-proof JSON (signed by Redwood key).
- Timeline: once agreement signed, prepare bundle (2 business days), run integrity verification (1 business day), transfer window (within next 2 business days) — so 3–5 business days total as Priya said.

Attachment: log_sample_manifest.csv

If you prefer an encrypted archive export (customer key), we can support that too; that path adds ~1 day for key exchange and validation.

— Marcus
Marcus Lin
Senior Reliability Engineer | Redwood Inference
From: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwoodinference.com>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwoodinference.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>, Acme Health Security Ops <security_ops@acmehealth.com>
Date: Wed, 06 Jun 2028 09:17:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Post-incident logs — retention window and escrow option

Thanks Priya / Marcus. A few legal/controls notes we need to document before any escrow or transfer:

1) Chain of custody: every transfer must include a chain-of-custody record with employee ids of Redwood operators, timestamps, and transfer hashes. We will attach a chain-of-custody form to the Evidence Transfer Agreement.
2) Scope-limited extracts: Acme may request redacted extracts (PII masked) in lieu of full raw logs; Redwood should provide both a full-hold and a redacted-extract path and clearly note the differences in the manifest.
3) Retention beyond 90 days: retention extensions must be requested in writing with business justification; we will log extension approvals and retain that as part of the audit trail.
4) Export controls & cross-border: confirm that escrow recipient (SecureAudit) will store artifacts in us-east-1 for Acme; if Acme requests EU residency we need a separate workflow.

I'll circulate a short Evidence Transfer Agreement draft for signature — Priya, Marcus, please review language on chain of custody and redaction options.

Mina Haddad
Senior Counsel, Compliance | Redwood Inference
From: Jane Doe <jane.doe@acmehealth.com>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwoodinference.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>, Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, 07 Jun 2028 11:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Post-incident logs — retention window and escrow option

Thanks — this is helpful. Acme would like the following so we can close our audit:

- Proceed with the 90-day administrative hold.
- Please prepare the Evidence Transfer Agreement with the SecureAudit S3 bucket as primary escrow recipient (us-east-1).
- Provide the signed transfer manifest and SHA256 hashes. We also need the chain-of-custody form that Mina mentioned.
- For expediency, can you send a DocuSign link for the agreement and an expected calendar date for transfer (we're targeting next Thu 6/15 if possible)?

We prefer the cross-account S3 copy to avoid creating a downloadable archive. If Redwood needs Acme to approve any additional paperwork, flag it to me directly.

Best,
Jane Doe
Principal Security Engineer | Acme Health
security_ops@acmehealth.com
